Position Summary
Driving advanced enterprise network architecture, wireless infrastructure deployment, and secure routing systems for a premier government project in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Go Ahead Consulting is actively seeking an accomplished Network Engineer (Cisco Wireless) for a permanent professional engagement.
In this vital network engineering role, you will architect, configure, and optimize mission-critical Cisco wireless networks, enterprise routing and switching, load balancers, quality of service (QoS) frameworks, and SD-WAN architectures.
Bringing specialized expertise in enterprise networking and Cisco wireless solutions, you will empower public-sector digital infrastructure to achieve uncompromised connectivity, high availability, and fault-tolerant data transmission.
This prestigious career opportunity offers competitive remuneration, high technical visibility, and exceptional professional growth within a premier global IT recruitment and consulting enterprise.

Detailed
As a Network Engineer (Cisco Wireless) supporting government project initiatives through Go Ahead Consulting in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, you will take full operational, architectural, and tactical ownership of wireless network design, routing protocols, load balancing, QoS implementation, and SD-WAN optimization.
Your day-to-day responsibilities include deploying Cisco wireless controllers and access points, configuring enterprise routers and switches, managing traffic load balancers, tuning QoS policies for mission-critical applications, and ensuring strict compliance with government security baselines.

Key Responsibilities
• Architect, configure, deploy, and maintain robust enterprise Cisco wireless networks, controllers, and access points across government facilities.

• Design and manage complex enterprise routing and switching protocols (BGP, OSPF, EIGRP) across multi-site environments.

• Configure and optimize enterprise load balancers to ensure high availability and efficient traffic distribution for critical applications.

• Implement and fine‑tune Quality of Service (QoS) policies to prioritize voice, video, and mission-critical data streams.

• Deploy, manage, and troubleshoot Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) architectures for enhanced multi-branch connectivity.

• Perform rigorous network performance tuning, latency reduction, throughput optimization, and fault isolation.

• Collaborate seamlessly with cross-functional IT infrastructure, cybersecurity, and government project management squads.

• Maintain comprehensive network topology diagrams, routing configurations, firewall rulebases, and incident runbooks.

Required Qualifications & Skills
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Telecommunications Engineering, Information Technology, or related discipline.

• Minimum of 5+ years of progressive professional experience in enterprise network engineering and infrastructure deployment.

• Strong, demonstrable hands‑on professional expertise in Cisco Wireless networking, WLCs, and enterprise Wi-Fi deployments.

• Comprehensive working knowledge and practical proficiency in enterprise routing and switching, BGP, OSPF, and VLAN architectures.

• Deep practical experience configuring and managing load balancers, traffic management, and Quality of Service (QoS) frameworks.

• Solid practical grasp of SD-WAN design, implementation, and multi-site network integration.

• Proven analytical, troubleshooting, and cross-functional stakeholder communication capabilities.

jobs.job_title: Network Engineer - AI Infrastructure, RDMA & Storage
jobs.job_description:
Network Engineer - AI Infrastructure, RDMA & Storage
• Engineering
• APAC
• Full-time

Description
VAST Data is the data platform company for the AI era. We build enterprise software infrastructure to capture, catalog, refine, enrich, and protect massive datasets, and make them available for real-time data analysis and AI training and inference. Designed from the ground up to make AI simple to deploy and manage, VAST takes the cost and complexity out of deploying enterprise and AI infrastructure across data center, edge, and cloud.

About the Role :

The fastest system in the world is only as fast as the network under it. As a Network Engineer in VAST's Field Engineering organization, you define how VAST connects to the world: the reference architectures, validated switch configurations, and RDMA fabric designs every customer deployment is built on.

This is a design and research role, not a support queue. You will build and run the lab where new switches, NICs, and network operating systems are qualified before they ever reach a customer. You will investigate why a fabric behaves differently at 800G than it did at 100G, and turn the answer into a standard the whole field organization uses. When a strategic customer hits something nobody has seen before, you reproduce it, explain it, and make sure it never happens to the next customer.

You will work across R&D, QA, Support, Product, and customer engineering teams, and directly with networking vendors including NVIDIA, Arista, Cisco, and Juniper. The work sits where AI infrastructure is hardest: GPU fabrics, lossless Ethernet, and storage protocols moving at line rate.

Requirements
What a Day in the Life Looks Like :

Design the Architecture: Define reference network architectures for VAST deployments: L2 and L3 fabrics, BGP and EVPN/VXLAN designs, RoCEv2 and QoS policy. Decide what \"good\" looks like, then write it down so the field can execute it consistently.

Own the Lab: Build and run validation environments for switch qualification, interoperability testing, performance characterization, and reproduction of customer issues. Your lab is where we find problems before customers do.

Qualify the Ecosystem: Evaluate new switches, network operating systems, and NICs from NVIDIA, Arista, Cisco, Juniper, and others. Work directly with vendor engineering teams to close gaps and certify what works.

Solve What Nobody Else Can: Chase complex problems across the full path between GPUs, fabric, and storage. Congestion, packet loss, MTU, latency, PFC and ECN behavior under real load. Root cause it, then fix it at the source.

Turn Findings into Product: Feed what you learn back into VAST, as documented best practice, as automation, and as direct input to R&D on what the platform should do differently.

Professional Experience & Skills

• Strong data center networking fundamentals - CCNP level or equivalent hands-on experience

• Solid command of BGP and L3 routing: eBGP/iBGP, ECMP, route policy, multipath, BGP-based fabrics

• Hands-on experience designing and troubleshooting both L2 and L3 data center networks

• Real troubleshooting ability across layers - routing, ARP/ND, MTU, congestion, packet loss, latency

• Working knowledge of Linux networking: interfaces, VLANs, routing tables, namespaces, MTU

• Comfort with tcpdump, Wireshark, iperf, and the standard diagnostic toolkit

• The instinct to build a lab and reproduce a problem rather than theorize about it

• Clear technical writing - your designs and findings are only useful if others can follow them
